pages.title: Overview
pages.body: Camera Journey shows how to make autonomous camera motion readable. A closed Catmull-Rom spline is drawn as a cyan rail through a neon pillar field, with waypoint markers showing the path the camera follows. A glowing central object and orbiters stay near the middle of the tour, while the visible rail and pillars make the camera movement obvious rather than looking like a static object. Pressing C hands control back to OrbitControls; Space rejoins the scripted path.

pages.title: Data Arrays: Path, Rings & Orbiters
pages.body: `PATH_POINTS` defines the closed camera rail as plain coordinates. `RING_DATA` encodes three torus rings as objects with color, dimensions, tilt, and signed spin speed, while `ORBITER_DATA` describes the small spheres circling the central object. Keeping these values as data makes the scene easy to reshape without rewriting setup logic.

pages.title: Building the Scene
pages.body: Setup disables OrbitControls so the scripted path starts immediately. `buildPillarField` creates a field of instanced columns with deterministic heights, giving the viewer a fixed reference frame. `buildPathRail` turns the path points into a visible Catmull-Rom curve and waypoint markers. The core sphere, rings, and orbiters then provide a bright subject for the camera to frame during the tour.

pages.title: Camera Path Math
pages.body: `updateCamera` samples the spline by elapsed time, then samples a second point slightly ahead on the path to create a look target. That look target is pulled toward the scene center so the central object remains framed while the pillars and visible rail show forward motion. When manual mode is active, the scripted camera update is skipped and OrbitControls owns the view until Space rejoins the path.

pages.title: Teardown
pages.body: Teardown removes the keydown listener and HUD, then re-enables OrbitControls so the next example starts with normal mouse navigation. This is deliberate because Camera Journey suppresses controls in setup.
